root_cause.text: The driver fails to re-anchor URBs after each completion because the USB core unanchors URBs before invoking the completion callback, so URBs that are resubmitted are not included in the `rx_submitted` anchor list and are never freed by `usb_kill_anchored_urbs()` in `gs_can_close()`, causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly explains that "the USB framework unanchors the URB before the complete function is called," and the patch adds `usb_anchor_urb(urb, &parent->rx_submitted)` inside `gs_usb_receive_bulk_callback()` to re-anchor the URB before resubmission.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the initial commit, the receive callback function `gs_usb_recieve_bulk_callback` resubmits the URB at the `resubmit_urb` label without re-anchoring it to `parent->rx_submitted`. According to the vulnerability description, the USB core unanchors URBs before invoking the completion callback, so the resubmitted URB is no longer in the anchor list. Consequently, when `gs_can_close` calls `usb_kill_anchored_urbs(&parent->rx_submitted)`, these resubmitted URBs are not killed and remain allocated, causing a memory leak. No re-anchor call exists in this version.
